patterns.name: ioctl_surface
patterns.rationale: ioctl handlers often expose complex user-controlled state transitions.

patterns.name: copy_from_user
patterns.rationale: user-to-kernel data movement is a frequent memory corruption entrypoint.

patterns.name: copy_to_user
patterns.rationale: kernel-to-user transfers are a strong info-leak signal.

patterns.name: user_pointer
patterns.rationale: explicit user pointer handling usually marks trust boundaries.

patterns.name: allocator
patterns.rationale: allocation around user input often couples to lifetime and bounds bugs.

patterns.name: free_path
patterns.rationale: free paths near user-triggerable flows increase UAF and double-free risk.

patterns.name: refcount
patterns.rationale: reference counting mistakes are common kernel CVE material.

patterns.name: size_math
patterns.rationale: length arithmetic and struct sizing are strong overflow indicators.

patterns.name: memcpy_family
patterns.rationale: buffer movement around user-derived lengths can lead to overwrite or leak.

patterns.name: lockless_or_racy
patterns.rationale: locking primitives help surface race windows when paired with frees or refs.

patterns.name: bpf_surface
patterns.rationale: BPF and packet processing frequently expose rich attacker-controlled state.

patterns.name: capability_gate
patterns.rationale: authorization checks nearby can indicate privilege-boundary mistakes.

patterns.name: warning_marker
patterns.rationale: existing invariant checks often cluster around historically fragile code.
